title.narrative: SHE-ACT: Safeguarding Her Empowerment – Action for Community Transformation.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project will be implemented through a consortium approach by two leading national women-led NGOs—Women Empowerment-Action (WE-Action) and Education for Sustainable Development (ESD). These organizations will combine their respective expertise and proven capacities to address the high protection risks and the prevalence of Sexual and Gender-Based Violence (SGBV) in the conflict-affected districts of Debremarkos, Michakel, and Mertolemariam in the Amhara Region.ltbrgtPreliminary data obtained from local government structures in these target areas indicates that SGBV survivors face significant challenges in accessing appropriate and survivor-centered services due to fragmented response infrastructures. Access to justice and tailored support remains severely constrained. To validate and deepen this understanding, the project will conduct a comprehensive protection risk and SGBV analysis during the inception phase.ltbrgtThe proposed intervention aims to improve SGBV prevention and response mechanisms and provide timely, dignified, and survivor-centered support to SGBV survivors in the three targeted districts. The project will directly reach 29,106 individuals—including women, girls, men, and boys—with 10% (2911) identified as persons with disabilities and other doubly vulnerable groups. Services will include mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), case management, distribution of dignity kits, and emergency cash assistance.ltbrgtThe project’s four interlinked outputs include:ltbrgt(1) Ensuring timely and appropriate support to GBV survivors and at-risk women and girls through case management, psychosocial support, emergency assistance, and provision of age- and context-appropriate dignity kits.ltbrgt(2) Strengthening referral pathways and coordination among SGBV service providers to deliver holistic, survivor-centered services.ltbrgt(3) Enhancing GBV prevention and response through improved service delivery and increased community awareness, including engaging men and boys.ltbrgt(4) Reducing institutional protection risks and strengthening the capacity of actors involved in SGBV response.ltbrgtBoth WE-Action and ESD have demonstrated experience in humanitarian response and long-standing presence in the region. They have successfully implemented projects in conflict-sensitive contexts, including the EHF 2024 First Standard Allocation in East and West Gojam zones. Their operational approach incorporates conflict-sensitive strategies that ensure the safety of staff and access to hard-to-reach areas.ltbrgtThe two organizations are Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS) Alliance members and actively participate in the Protection Cluster, adhering to the nine commitments for quality and accountability in humanitarian programming. Their technical expertise, community trust, and established partnerships with local actors position them well to coordinate and deliver impactful protection and SGBV services.ltbrgtA comprehensive risk mitigation strategy is in place, with a risk register regularly updated to reflect evolving challenges around security, financial management, and protection. The project applies an intersectional approach that considers the diverse identities and needs of affected populations. By targeting individuals based on vulnerability and promoting inclusivity, the project will benefit both direct and indirect beneficiaries within the broader community.ltbrgtSGBV is not only a gross violation of human rights but also a significant economic and social burden that undermines national development and the well-being of society. This justifies the request for a total budget of USD 450,000 to support this initiative under the 2025 EHF First Standard Allocation for the Amhara region and contribute to the national agenda of reducing SGBV and strengthening protection systems.ltbrgtlt/pgt
